title: Same Recipe, Different Fate: The Training Recipe's Effect on Safety Erosion from Benign Fine-Tuning Depends on the Model Family
description: Benign fine-tuning can erode safety, but reported effects vary widely. We compare six instruct models from OLMo-2, Llama-3 and Qwen2.5, at about 1B and at 7–8B, using LoRA on 4,800 Dolly rows with three seeds per main recipe cell. Erosion E is the rise in Qwen3Guard's Unsafe share of 600 sampled answers to 200 development harm prompts; HarmBench is a second judge. At 1B, a Scheduled recipe (warmup, cosine decay and token-mean loss) lowers OLMo-2-1B's mean erosion from +45.1 to +28.8 pp, compared with +59.3 to +57.1 for Llama-3.2-1B and +71.9 to +73.9 for Qwen2.5-1.5B. Both OLMo family-interaction intervals exclude zero on both judges, but OLMo's over-refusal rises by 11.7 pp. The pre-registered OLMo-versus-Llama replication at 7–8B is inconclusive. Qwen2.5-7B's mean erosion falls from +78.1 to +68.9 pp; its interaction with OLMo excludes zero on Qwen3Guard only. Halving the learning rate lowers mean erosion in OLMo-7B and Llama-8B, without establishing equal effects. Under one recipe, OLMo erodes least and Qwen most at both sizes. Dark–light fiction differences lie within wide pre-registered margins. A blind human read suggests the Unsafe label mostly tracks lost refusal. All results are development evidence; we report every screened setting and the judges' limits.
notes: 24 pages, 2 figures; includes appendices. Development evidence. Preprint; not peer reviewed.
publication_status: Prepared locally; not deposited or published on Zenodo.
